data.headline: Cambium Introduces a Viability-Governed Operator for AI-Powered Ventures
data.subheadline: The Infinite Game Engine coordinates bounded specialist agents while preserving founder authority, mission continuity, and replayable evidence.
data.lead_paragraph: [CITY], [DATE] — Thoughtseed today unveiled Cambium, a proposed venture operating layer designed to coordinate finite AI systems around a business's ability to continue. Built for solo founders and small venture operators, Cambium wakes on real events, evaluates explicit viability bounds, proposes the next bounded specialist run, and keeps paid or irreversible actions behind a founder-controlled gate.

body_paragraphs.content: Existing agent systems can mint brands, build software, publish campaigns, and complete operational tasks. Those are finite games with appropriate end states. Cambium addresses the layer between them: carrying a venture's vision, current mission, constraints, authority, and learning from one completed run to the next.

Cambium treats revenue as operating fuel and solvency as a bound rather than maximizing activity or growth as a terminal objective. The system is designed around observable margins such as solvency, mission coherence, legal and ethical limits, and founder capacity. It does not claim to compute an exact high-dimensional viability kernel.

Reversible and pre-authorized work can proceed through specialist systems. Paid, irreversible, identity-changing, data-moving, or externally representative actions remain fail-closed until the designated founder authority approves them.

Cambium's doctrine calls for typed, event-sourced world-state and receipts that name the triggering event, evidence, current state, authority, decision, and result. Public capability statements will be released only with current production receipts.

The proposed first experience is deliberately small: map one venture, name one viability bound, admit one evidence-bearing event, and replay one governed decision. Broader availability, product readiness, and commercial terms remain subject to owner approval and acceptance evidence.

The Infinite Game Engine coordinates bounded specialist agents while preserving founder authority, mission continuity, and replayable evidence.

Cambium treats revenue as operating fuel and solvency as a bound rather than maximizing activity or growth as a terminal objective. Its doctrine uses observable margins such as solvency, mission coherence, legal and ethical limits, and founder capacity. The system does not claim to compute an exact high-dimensional viability kernel.

Reversible and pre-authorized work can proceed through specialist systems. Paid, irreversible, identity-changing, data-moving, or externally representative actions remain fail-closed until the designated founder authority approves them.

The proposed first experience is deliberately small: map one venture, name one viability bound, admit one evidence-bearing event, and replay one governed decision. Availability, acceptance, pricing, and release timing remain unannounced.
